title: IEEE SPS Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment Challenge
terms:
1. General Rules

  • Eligibility: This competition is open to all researchers, students, and developers worldwide.
  • One Account Per Team: Participants may not sign up for multiple accounts to bypass submission limits. Doing so will result in disqualification.
  • No Private Sharing: Private sharing of code or data outside of teams is not permitted.

2. Data Usage

  • The datasets provided (distorted and reference images) are for academic and research purposes only.
  • Participants are not allowed to use the dataset for commercial products without permission.

3. Submission & Integrity

  • Honor Code: You agree not to attempt to reverse-engineer the ground truth labels or "probe" the leaderboard excessively.
  • Final Decision: The organizers reserve the right to disqualify any team that violates these rules or the spirit of the competition.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge

Welcome to the **Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge**! This is the **2nd** MoIQA Challenge, affiliated to the **IEEE SPS Challenge Program**. The competition focuses on the machine-oriented perceptual quality of visual media.

## Background

With the development of Embodied AI, machines have replaced humans as the main consumers of visual media, yet existing Image Quality Assessment (IQA) metrics remain focused on humans and overlook machine task utility. To address this gap, we introduce the Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge. This challenge aims to advance reliable image understanding for machine preference and support robust Embodied AI applications.

---

## The Challenge

The dataset covers three major types of visual media: **AI-Generated Images (AIGI)**, **Natural Scene Images (NSI)**, and **Screen Content Images (SCI)**. In total, the dataset contains **100 reference images** and **3,000 distorted images**, where each distorted image is generated from one reference image by applying one of **30 distortion types (T01–T30)** at one of **5 severity levels (S1–S5)**.

Participants are asked to predict a **quality score** for each distorted image. The ground-truth quality scores are annotated on a **1–5 scale**, reflecting the machine-oriented perceptual quality of the visual content. The training set is released **with** ground-truth labels, while the validation and test sets are released **without** labels — participants submit their predictions to the CodaBench platform for evaluation.

---

## Competition Phases

### Development Phase
* **Objective**: Train and refine your model on the released training set (with ground-truth quality labels and reference images), and predict the quality scores of the validation set (released without labels or reference images). Predictions are submitted to CodaBench for live ranking.

### Test Phase
* **Objective**: Predict the quality scores of the held-out test set (released without labels or reference images). The final ranking is based on this phase. For both phases, prediction is performed directly on the distorted images, and submissions may be **continuous scores** — integer ratings are not required.

---

## Evaluation

Submissions are evaluated by the correlation between the predicted quality scores and the ground truth:

* **Pearson Linear Correlation Coefficient (PLCC)**: Measures the linear relationship between the predicted scores and the ground truth.
* **Spearman Rank-Order Correlation Coefficient (SRCC)**: Measures the monotonic relationship (ranking consistency) between the predicted scores and the ground truth.

The final ranking score is the **mean of PLCC and SRCC**, which is the only column shown on the leaderboard.

---

## Contact

For any inquiries, please reach out to:

* **Email**: lcysyzxdxc@sjtu.edu.cn

pages.content:
## 1. Download Data ### **Part A: Training Dataset** * **Content**: 2,100 distorted images (`dis/`), 70 reference images (`ref/`), and ground-truth `labels.csv` (`index`, `quality`) * **Link**: [Link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19dpE3zHEdOyebAvdefXiubCX6Tu6O4lX/view?usp=drive_link) ### **Part B: Validation Dataset** * **Content**: 600 distorted images. Released **without** labels or reference images. * **Link**: [Link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1n2bOoESGAe08sThzRU5ZUdLbFwqzFRgo/view?usp=sharing) ### **Part C: Test Dataset** * **Content**: 300 distorted images. Released **without** labels or reference images. * **Link**: Coming soon ### **Part D: Starting Kit** * **Content**: Submission template (`submission.tsv`) & random-score generator * **Link**: [Link](https://www.codabench.org/datasets/download/714130ad-feea-4dfa-81aa-b432901c80a0/) > > **Submission Format Example** > > Download the **Submission Template** to see a working example of the submission structure. --- ## 2. Dataset Statistics The dataset consists of **100 reference images** and **3,000 distorted images** in total, covering three major types of visual media: **AI-Generated Images (AIGI)**, **Natural Scene Images (NSI)**, and **Screen Content Images (SCI)**.

   **Distortion Types**: 30 types (T01–T30). **Severity Levels**: 5 levels (S1–S5); each (reference image, distortion type) pair is annotated at one severity level. **Splits**: Train 70 refs / 2,100 distorted · Validation 20 refs / 600 distorted · Test 10 refs / 300 distorted. Splits are grouped **by reference image** (all distorted variants of one reference image stay in the same split). --- ## 3. Data Format All images are provided as **PNG files** (RGB), organized per split: * **Training package**: `dis/` (distorted images) + `ref/` (reference images) + `labels.csv`. * **Validation / Test packages**: distorted images only (no reference images, no labels). * **Naming Convention**: Reference Image: `{category}_{model}_{id}.png` (e.g., `AIGI_DALLE3_003.png`). Distorted Image: `{reference_name}_T{distortion_type}_S{severity}.png` (e.g., `AIGI_DALLE3_003_T01_S4.png`). ### Label Description (Training Set) * `labels.csv` columns: * **`index`**: The distorted image filename (including the `.png` extension), e.g. `AIGI_DALLE3_003_T01_S4.png`. * **`quality`**: **[Target]** The ground-truth quality score, annotated on a **1–5 scale**. Higher scores indicate better machine-oriented perceptual quality. ### Prediction Task (Validation / Test) * For each released `index`, participants predict the `quality` score. * **Submissions may be any continuous values** — integer ratings are not required. * Submissions are made through the CodaBench platform; see the **Evaluation & Submission** page for the exact format. ## 4. Additional Training Data * **Simulation Track:** [MPD Dataset](https://github.com/lcysyzxdxc/MPD) * **Real-Robot Track:** [EmbodiedIQA Dataset](https://github.com/aiben-ch/EmbodiedIQA) *If you use these datasets, please adhere to the following citation formats:* **Simulation Data Citation:** ```bibtex @inproceedings{simdata, author = {Li, Chunyi and Tian, Yuan and Ling, Xiaoyue and Zhang, Zicheng and Duan, Haodong and Wu, Haoning and Jia, Ziheng and Liu, Xiaohong and Min, Xiongkuo and Lu, Guo and Lin, Weisi and Zhai, Guangtao}, title = {Image Quality Assessment: From Human to Machine Preference}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)}, month = {June}, year = {2025}, pages = {7570-7581} } ``` **Real-Robot Data Citation:** ```bibtex @inproceedings{realdata, title={Image Quality Assessment for Embodied {AI}}, author={Chunyi Li and Jiahao Xiao and Jianbo Zhang and Farong Wen and Zicheng Zhang and Yuan Tian and Xiangyang Zhu and Xiaohong Liu and Zhengxue Cheng and Weisi Lin and Guangtao Zhai}, booktitle={The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations}, year={2026}, url={https://openreview.net/forum?id=azj53PLJRL} } ```

pages.title: Evaluation & Submission
pages.content:
## 1. Submission Format To participate in the Preliminary Round, you must submit a **ZIP file** containing a single TSV file named **`submission.tsv`**. The file must follow the specific formatting and column requirements. **File Structure:** * **Archive**: `submission.zip` * **Content**: `submission.tsv` **TSV Header Requirements:** The TSV file must include the following two columns: 1. **index**: The unique identifier for each distorted image (the image filename, including the `.png` extension). 2. **quality**: Your predicted quality score for each image (floating-point value). **Note:** Predictions may be any **continuous values** — integer ratings are not required. **Example TSV Content:**
index quality
AIGI_DALLE3_003_T01_S4.png 3.1246
AIGI_DALLE3_003_T02_S4.png 2.0327
AIGI_DALLE3_003_T03_S5.png 2.9875
... ...
> **Test Phase Submission Format Example** > > Download the **Test Submission Template** to see a working example of the **test phase** submission structure. **(待发布 / Coming soon)** --- ## 2. Evaluation Metrics Submissions are evaluated based on their correlation with the Ground Truth (GT) scores. We use two primary statistical metrics to assess the accuracy of your predictions: * **Pearson Linear Correlation Coefficient (PLCC)**: Measures the linear relationship between the predicted scores and the ground truth. * **Spearman Rank-Order Correlation Coefficient (SRCC)**: Measures the monotonic relationship (ranking consistency) between the predicted scores and the ground truth. --- ## 3. Leaderboard Ranking The competition features a single ranking track. * **Quality Score (PLCC & SRCC Mean)** * Evaluated as the mean of PLCC and SRCC computed between the predicted quality scores and the ground truth. This is the only column shown on the leaderboard. --- ## 4. Important Notes * **Consistency**: Ensure the `index` column matches the Test Set exactly. Any missing rows or mismatched indices will result in a submission error. * **Encoding**: Do not include image data in your submission; only the predicted scores are required. * **Precision**: We recommend providing scores with at least 4 decimal places for better ranking granularity.
